source_text: ἡμῖν τῶν ἁγίων ὑποδηλοῦν. Κλίβανος γὰρ καὶ ἐσχάρα, καὶ μὴν καὶ τὸ μύλῳ καταλεπτύνεσθαι, σημεῖά που πάντως εἶεν ἂν συντριβῆς τε καὶ πόνου δοκιμαζομένων ὡς διὰ πυρός. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ κεκράγασι, τὴν οὕτως εὐκλεᾶ διαστείχοντες τρίβον· «Ὅτι ἐδοκίμασας ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς, ἐπύρωσας ἡμᾶς, ὡς πυροῦται τὸ ἀργύριον.» Ψάλλει δέ που καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος ἡμῖν Δαβίδ· «Καρδίαν συντετριμμένην καὶ τεταπεινωμένην ὁ Θεὸς οὐκ ἐξουδενώσει.» Ἀλλ' ὅτι τοῖς ὧδε πεπονηκόσι, τὸ ἐν εὐωδίᾳ γενέσθαι Χριστοῦ, πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἕποιτο ἂν εἰκότως· καὶ μὴν ὅτι καὶ τὸ ἐλεεῖσθαι δεῖν, καὶ τῇ τοῦ Πνεύματος χάριτι πλουσίως καταπιαίνεσθαι, σαφὲς ἂν γένοιτο τὴν τοῦ λιβάνου τε καὶ ἐλαίου περινοοῦντι χρείαν. Ἢ γὰρ οὐχὶ λεπτῶν αἰνιγμάτων ὑποψίαι πως ἡμῖν καὶ σκιαὶ τὰ ἐν νόμῳ; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἑαυτοὺς μὲν ἄρα προσοίσομεν τῷ Θεῷ, κατανεκρούμενοι τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, καὶ τὸν ἱερὸν τουτονὶ νοητῶς ὑπομένοντες θάνατον, ζῶντές γε μὴν τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, καὶ ὡς ἐν τάξει χαριστηρίων τὴν ἰδίαν αὐτῷ ζωὴν ἀπονέμοντες εὐκλεᾶ τε καὶ ἀνεπίπληκτον, καὶ τοῖς εἰς φιλοθεΐαν αὐχήμασιν εὐπρεπῆ. Τοῦτό τοι σαφῶς καὶ δι' ἑτέρων εἰσόμεθα νόμων. Γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν τῷ Λευϊτικῷ· «Ἐὰν δὲ θυσία σωτηρίου τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἐὰν μὲν ἐκ τῶν βοῶν αὐτὸ προσαγάγῃ, ἐάν τε ἄρσεν, ἐάν τε θῆλυ, ἄμωμον προσάξει αὐτὸ ἔναντι Κυρίου· καὶ ἐπιθήσει τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ δώρου, καὶ σφάξει αὐτὸ ἐναντίον Κυρίου παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου. Καὶ προσχεοῦσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἀαρὼν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὸ αἷμα ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων κύκλῳ. Καὶ προσάξουσιν ἀπὸ τῆς θυσίας τοῦ σωτηρίου κάρπωμα Κυρίῳ, τὸ στέαρ τὸ κατακαλύπτον τὴν κοιλίαν, καὶ πᾶν τὸ στέαρ τὸ ἐπὶ τῆς κοιλίας· καὶ τοὺς δύο νεφροὺς, καὶ τὸ στέαρ τὸ ἐπ' αὐτῶν, τὸ ἐπὶ τῶν μηρίων, καὶ τὸν λοβὸν τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ ἥπατος σὺν τοῖς νεφροῖς περιελεῖ· καὶ ἀνοίσουσιν αὐτὰ οἱ υἱοὶ Ἀαρὼν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον ἐπὶ τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα ἐπὶ τὰ ξύλα, τὰ ἐπὶ τοῦ πυρὸς ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου· κάρπωμα, ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ.» Ἄμωμος τοίνυν ὁ μόσχος· καθαροὺς γὰρ εἶναι πρέπει, καὶ μώμου παντὸς ἰόντας ὡς ἀπωτάτω, τοὺς εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀναβαίνοντας τῷ Θεῷ. Ἐσφάζετο δὲ πρὸς αὐταῖς ταῖς θύραις τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, ἐπενηνεγμένων αὐτῷ τῶν χειρῶν τοῦ προσάγοντος. Καὶ τίς ὁ τοῦδε λόγος, εἴρηται σαφῶς. Ἀνεκομίζετο δὲ εἰς θυσίαν τὸ στέαρ τὸ ἐπὶ τῆς κοιλίας, καὶ οἱ δύο νεφροὶ, συνεξαιρουμένης αὐτοῖς τῆς ἐνούσης πιμελῆς, καὶ ὁ λοβὸς τοῦ ἥπατος. Καὶ ὑποφήνειεν ἂν, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, τὸ ἐπὶ τῆς κοιλίας στέαρ, τὴν οἱονεὶ φρενὸς εὐεξίαν, καὶ τὴν πιότητα τῶν σπλάγχνων ἐντεθραμμένων ἄριστα ταῖς διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος νοηταῖς χορηγίαις. Εὐτροφία μὲν γὰρ τοῖς ἀλόγοις ζώοις, καὶ μὴν καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρωπίνοις σώμασι τὸ καταπιαίνεσθαι προξενεῖ. Θείων δὲ χαρισμάτων πλουσιωτάτη μέθεξις, παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ τὴν
pass_a_gloss: [completing §8’s last sentence] to hint (ὑποδηλόω) to us … of the saints. For oven (κλίβανος) and grill (ἐσχάρα), and indeed being ground fine (καταλεπτύνομαι) with a mill (μύλος), would surely be signs (σημεῖα) of crushing (συντριβή) and toil (πόνος) of those being tested (δοκιμάζομαι) as through fire (ὡς διὰ πυρός). Therefore they have cried out (κράζω, pf.), walking through (διαστείχω) the path (τρίβος) so glorious (εὐκλεής): ‘For You tested (δοκιμάζω) us, O God, You fired/refined (πυρόω) us as silver (ἀργύριον) is fired.’ And the inspired David sings (ψάλλω): ‘A heart crushed (συντρίβω, pf. ptc.) and humbled (ταπεινόω) God will not set at nought (ἐξουδενόω).’ But that for those who have so toiled (πονέω) to come to be in the fragrance (εὐωδία) of Christ would fittingly follow in every way; and indeed that they must be shown mercy (ἐλεέομαι) and be richly fattened/enriched (καταπιαίνομαι) by the grace (χάρις) of the Spirit, would become clear to one considering (περινοέω) the use (χρεία) of the frankincense and oil. Or are not the things in law (τὰ ἐν νόμῳ) to us somehow suggestions (ὑποψίαι) and shadows (σκιαί) of fine riddles (λεπτὰ αἰνίγματα)? PALL.: Certainly. CYR.: Ourselves then we shall bring (προσφέρω) to God, being made dead (κατανεκρόομαι) to sin, and enduring (ὑπομένω) this sacred death spiritually/intelligibly (νοητῶς), but living to righteousness (ζῶντες τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ), according to what is written, and as in the rank (τάξις) of thank offerings (χαριστήρια) assigning (ἀπονέμω) to Him our own life, glorious and unreproachable (ἀνεπίπληκτος), and comely (εὐπρεπής) with the boasts/glories (αὐχήματα) toward love of God (φιλοθεΐα). This we shall know clearly through other laws too. For it is written in Leviticus: [Lev 3:1–5] if a sacrifice of salvation/deliverance (θυσία σωτηρίου) is his gift to the Lord, if from the oxen (βόες) he brings it, whether male or female, unblemished (ἄμωμος) he will bring it before the Lord; and he will lay the hands on the head of the gift and slaughter (σφάζω) it before the Lord beside the doors of the tent of witness (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου); and the sons of Aaron the priests will pour (προσχέω) the blood on the altar of the whole burnt offerings (ὁλοκαυτώματα) round about; and they will bring from the sacrifice of salvation an offering (κάρπωμα) to the Lord, the fat (στέαρ) covering the belly/entrails (κοιλία) and all the fat on the belly, and the two kidneys (νεφροί) and the fat on them, that on the thighs/loins (μηρία), and the lobe (λοβός) on the liver (ἧπαρ) with the kidneys he will remove (περιαιρέω); and the sons of Aaron the priests will carry them up onto the altar onto the whole burnt offerings onto the wood on the fire on the altar; an offering, a smell of fragrance (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας) to the Lord. Unblemished then the calf (μόσχος); for it befits those going up (ἀναβαίνω) to God for a smell of fragrance to be pure (καθαρός) and to go as far as possible from every blemish (μῶμος). It was slaughtered at the very doors of the holy tent, the hands of the one bringing having been laid on it. And what the reason (λόγος) of this is has been said clearly. There was carried up (ἀνακομίζω) for sacrifice the fat on the belly, and the two kidneys, the fat (πιμελή) in them being removed together (συνεξαιρέω) with them, and the lobe of the liver. And the fat on the belly would show (ὑποφαίνω), I think, the good condition (εὐεξία) as it were of the mind (φρήν), and the fatness (πιότης) of the inward parts (σπλάγχνα) nourished (ἐντρέφω) excellently on the intelligible provisions (νοηταὶ χορηγίαι) through the Spirit. For good feeding (εὐτροφία) brings about (προξενέω) being fattened (καταπιαίνομαι) for irrational animals (ἄλογα ζῷα) and indeed for human bodies; but a most rich participation (μέθεξις) in divine gifts (χαρίσματα) fills (ἐμπίπλημι, in §10) the mind (φρήν) of the saints with every good.
pass_b_english: Cyril: For the oven and the grill, and also being ground fine in a mill, would surely be signs of the crushing and toil of those who are tested as if by fire. That is why those who walk so glorious a path cry out: ‘For you have tested us, O God; you have tried us by fire, as silver is tried by fire’ (Psalm 66:10). And the inspired David sings to us somewhere: ‘A crushed and humbled heart God will not despise’ (Psalm 51:17). But that those who have toiled in this way would fittingly, and in every respect, come to be in the fragrance of Christ (2 Corinthians 2:15), and indeed that they must also receive mercy and be richly nourished by the grace of the Spirit, would be plain to anyone who considers the use of the frankincense and the oil. Or are not the things in the law, in a way, hints and shadows of subtle riddles for us?

Cyril: So we shall offer ourselves to God, being made dead to sin and undergoing this sacred death in a spiritual sense, yet living to righteousness, as it is written (1 Peter 2:24), and rendering to him, as a kind of thank offering, our own life, glorious and blameless, and made beautiful by all that love for God can boast of. We shall learn this clearly from other laws as well. For it is written in Leviticus: ‘If his gift to the Lord is a sacrifice of salvation, if he offers it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without blemish before the Lord. He shall lay his hands on the head of the gift and slaughter it before the Lord at the doors of the tent of witness. And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood on the altar of whole burnt offerings, all around. And from the sacrifice of salvation they shall bring as an offering to the Lord the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat that is on the entrails, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, which is on the loins; and he shall remove the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys. And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall carry them up to the altar, onto the whole burnt offerings, onto the wood that is on the fire on the altar; it is an offering, a fragrant aroma to the Lord’ (Leviticus 3:1–5).

The calf, then, is without blemish; for it is fitting that those who go up to God as a fragrant aroma should be pure and keep as far as they can from every blemish. It was slaughtered at the very doors of the holy tent, with the hands of the one offering it laid upon it; and what this means has been plainly stated already. The fat on the entrails was carried up for sacrifice, and the two kidneys, with the fat in them removed along with them, and the lobe of the liver. The fat on the entrails, I think, would signify the good health, so to speak, of the mind, and the richness of the inner parts when they have been nourished as well as can be on the spiritual provisions given through the Spirit. For good feeding makes brute animals, and human bodies too, grow fat; but a most abundant share in divine gifts fills the mind of the saints with every good thing.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

PG 68.1025. Boundary in: the opening words ἡμῖν τῶν ἁγίων ὑποδηλοῦν finish the sentence that begins at the end of section 8 and are rendered there (‘the passage seems … to hint to us at the approval the saints win…’); this section’s English therefore starts with the next sentence. Boundary out: the last sentence (Θείων δὲ χαρισμάτων πλουσιωτάτη μέθεξις, παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ τὴν …) is finished by the first words of section 10 (τῶν ἁγίων ἐμπίπλησι φρένα) and is rendered whole here (‘fills the mind of the saints with every good thing’). LXX renumbering: Psalm 65:10 LXX = Psalm 66:10; Psalm 50:19 LXX = Psalm 51:17. Πυρόω rendered ‘tried by fire’ to keep Cyril’s link with the oven and the fire. ‘Come to be in the fragrance of Christ’ echoes 2 Corinthians 2:15 (Χριστοῦ εὐωδία ἐσμέν); cited as a clear allusion. ‘Living to righteousness’ (ζῶντες τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ) with κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον matches 1 Peter 2:24 (τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ ζήσωμεν); dying to sin also recalls Romans 6:11 and offering ourselves Romans 12:1, but those are left uncited as looser echoes. ‘Tested as if by fire’ may echo 1 Peter 1:7 and ‘shadows’ in the law Hebrews 10:1; both doubtful, uncited. Ἐλεεῖσθαι (‘receive mercy’) plays on ἔλαιον (‘oil’); the pun cannot be kept in English. Καταπιαίνεσθαι (literally ‘be fattened’) is rendered ‘be richly enriched’ of the Spirit’s grace and ‘grow fat’ of animals and bodies. Θυσία σωτηρίου, the LXX name for the peace offering, is kept as ‘sacrifice of salvation’ in the quotation; χαριστήρια rendered ‘thank offering’. Σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου rendered ‘tent of witness’, as in sections 1–7. The law speaks of the herd (βόες); Cyril’s comment narrows it to ‘the calf’ (μόσχος). Κάρπωμα rendered ‘offering’ and ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας ‘a fragrant aroma’, matching sections 1–7. ‘What this means has been plainly stated already’ refers back to the laying on of hands discussed with the whole burnt offering earlier in the book.
